en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Chattupāhanavagga 86.
The Training Rule on the Hip-Girdle.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī was a frequent visitor to the family of a certain woman.
Then that woman said this to the bhikkhunī: “Come now, noble lady, give this waistband to the woman named so-and-so.”
Then that bhikkhunī thought,
"If I go taking it in my bowl, there will be a scandal for me," so she fastened it on and went along.
While she was on the carriage road, the string broke and they were scattered about.
People criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying:
“How can these bhikkhunīs wear a hip-string, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?
The bhikkhunīs heard those people criticizing, complaining, and spreading it about.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... they complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can a bhikkhunī wear a hip-string? ... [The Buddha asked:
"Is it true, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhunī wears a hip-string?"
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can a bhikkhunī wear a hip-string? …”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule:
‘If any nun wears a hip-cord, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whichever" means whichever such... "a bhikkhunī" means... [as before].
...pe... this is the nun intended in this context.
"Hip-cord" means any [garment] that reaches the hips.
"Should wear" means:
if she wears it even once, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense—
If she wears a waistband because of illness,
or if she is insane.
"By one who is a first offender":
thus ends the third training rule.
